featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this place for dinner, looking to try something different from the usual roti-sabji. We also wanted to keep it light with some veggies, so we started with the veg clear soup—it was flavorful and comforting. One suggestion: the vegetables in the soup were cut too large; finer cuts would enhance the experience.

We also ordered spring rolls. The taste was good, but the portion size was quite large and they were a bit too oily, which made it difficult for the three of us to finish.

Next, we tried the Fire Sizzler, which was a nice combination of buttered rice, Mexican-style vegetables in a rich gravy, and stuffed capsicum. The veggies served on the side were also fresh and well-cooked.

However, a couple of things could be improved: only sweet fennel (mukhwas) was available—regular saunf was missing, and the restroom was poorly maintained with no water and a strong bad odor.

Overall, the food was enjoyable and we appreciated the variety, but there's room for improvement in terms of cleanliness and a few small details.

featured_reviews.name: Bits of Bytes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Malgudi is a South Indian restaurant, but not your typical one. It has a unique spark that makes it stand out. Their innovative mocktail menu immediately caught my attention, and the food selection is extensive, with each dish well described. You’ll even find creative fusions like filter coffee panna cotta and The South Khow Suey.

Food and Drinks
- I tried the Zendo mocktail, which looked stunning with its purple top layer and white base. Each sip revealed a distinct taste as the layers blended.
- The Butter Pepper Garlic Water Chestnut was my absolute favorite. Even though I usually prefer non-vegetarian dishes, this preparation was so flavorful that I’d return just for it.
- The Sri Lankan Tamil Curry, rich with coconut and vegetables, reminded me of Thai curry but with a South Indian twist. It was beautifully paired with idiyappam.
- The Paneer Nellore Biryani was delightful, though I felt it could be improved with a lighter hand on the oil.
- For dessert, I ended with the indulgent Chocolate Pull-Up Cake, a sweet finale to the meal.

Ambience and Service
The interiors strike a balance between South Indian charm and modern design, creating a warm yet stylish atmosphere. Service was fast and attentive, with our server Aman Patel ensuring we had a wonderful dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Prachiti Gadekar
featured_reviews.review_text:

We started with their Hot Filter Kaapi—strong, authentic, and exactly what you expect. The Aam Berry Bae was refreshing and a fun seasonal twist.

For food, we tried the Aamras Podi Puri (a unique and delicious combo), Davangere Benne Podi Masala Dosa (buttery, crispy, and full of flavor), Podi Cheese Balls (perfectly indulgent), and Medu Vada which was soft inside and crisp outside—done just right.

And the showstopper? The Chocolate Pull Me Up dessert—easily the best way to end the meal. Rich, indulgent, and totally worth it!

featured_reviews.name: Muskan Poddar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Malgudi recently for a South Indian food craving, and it turned out to be such a satisfying experience. The place has a warm, simple vibe that instantly reminds you of authentic South Indian eateries, nothing too fancy, just comforting and inviting.

Coming to the food, everything felt genuinely authentic and full of flavor. From perfectly crisp dosas to soft, fluffy idlis and rich, comforting sambhar, every dish hit the right spot. The chutneys were fresh and well-balanced, which honestly made all the difference.

Service was quick and efficient, and the staff was polite throughout. It’s the kind of place you’d go back to when you’re craving no-nonsense, delicious South Indian food.

Definitely worth a visit if you’re around Lower Parel and in the mood for something simple, comforting, and satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Twinkle Jasani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Malgudi by Shankar Mahadevan recently, looking for South Indian food that’s slightly different from the usual.

The ambience is warm and rooted, with a modern touch that doesn’t feel forced. It’s a comfortable space to sit and enjoy a relaxed meal.

Started with the coconut cold brew, which was refreshing and easily one of the highlights. The benne podi dosa was good and comforting, though not exceptional.

The cheese podi bombs were interesting but could’ve used more spice and flavour depth. On the other hand, the butter pepper water chestnuts were very well balanced and a standout dish.

The chilli paneer curry was flavourful and quite spicy, so definitely something to keep in mind if you prefer milder food.

Ended with the filter coffee panna cotta, which was a nice, light dessert to finish the meal.

Overall, a mix of hits and a few misses, but worth trying for a slightly different take on South Indian cuisine.

featured_reviews.name: Ayush Bhandari
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a spot where traditional South Indian soul meets a modern, aesthetic vibe, Malgudi in Lower Parel is a masterclass in culinary harmony. Curated by the legendary Shankar Mahadevan, the restaurant feels less like a typical eatery and more like a carefully composed melody—vibrant, comforting, and full of character.
The ambience hits you first; it’s thoughtfully designed with a clean, aesthetic appeal that makes it perfect for a relaxed weekend brunch or a stylish dinner.
The Food: From Classic to Creative
The menu takes you on a journey through Karnataka and beyond, elevating humble staples into gourmet experiences.
Podi Cheese Balls: The spice of the podi cuts through the richness of the cheese, creating a crunchy, gooey delight that’s hard to stop at just one.
Ghee Podi Thate Idli: This was a standout. The idli was incredibly soft, acting as the perfect canvas for the fragrant, nutty podi and a generous dousing of ghee.
Davangere Benne Podi Dosa: True to its roots, this dosa was buttery (*benne*) and crisp, with the podi adding a layer of depth that reminded us why this regional specialty is so iconic.
Mulbagal Legacy Cheese Masala Dosa: The addition of cheese modernized the legacy recipe without overshadowing the traditional masala. Beverages:
Mango Berry Matcha: A vibrant, fruity twist on matcha that felt light and refreshing—a great palate cleanser between the buttery dosas.
Coconut Cold Brew Coffee: Smooth and tropical. The natural sweetness of the coconut milk paired beautifully with the bold kick of the cold brew.
Desserts:
You cannot leave without trying the Filter Kaffi Panna Cotta. It’s a brilliant nod to South Indian coffee culture, with a silky texture and a deep caffeine punch. The Chocolate Pull-Up Cake added a bit of "Instagrammable" drama to the table—decadent, rich, and the perfect end for any chocolate lover.

Malgudi isn't just about the name behind it; the food truly speaks for itself. It captures the "Legacy" of South India while dressing it up for the modern Lower Parel.

featured_reviews.name: Kunal Merchant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Really enjoyed our meal at Shenoy’s. The food consistently delivers on quality and authenticity.

We had the Rassa Chicken, Prawns Ghee Roast with bhakri, and fried bombil as a starter. My dining partner ordered the Konkan thali, which was excellent. Our waiter, Naeem, suggested ordering polis with the prawns ghee roast; great recommendation, it paired beautifully. Their Ghee Roast preparations are the best I have had in Mumbai ( though it is a close call) and their Rassa Chicken has the potential to become my new Butter Chicken. The Fried Bombil is a new improved version - crispier than before and serious contender to be the best fried Bombil in Bombay.

Service was attentive without being intrusive. Naeem was switched on, friendly, and made all the right suggestions.

What stands out is the care in the cooking, you can genuinely taste the authenticity and effort in every dish. Shenoy’s has become one of those rare places that sets a benchmark for Konkan food. I see myself becoming a regular. Highly recommended for anyone interested in the cuisine.

featured_reviews.name: Himanshi Patel
featured_reviews.review_text: Café Muthuswami in Dadar is a cozy spot that brings authentic South Indian flavors to life. Known for its crispy dosas, soft idlis, and rich, aromatic filter coffee, every bite feels comforting and nostalgic. The ambiance is simple yet inviting, perfect for casual catch-ups or a relaxed solo meal. Service is quick, and the food quality is consistently impressive. Whether you’re craving a hearty breakfast or a light evening snack, this café delivers on both taste and experience. A must-visit for anyone who loves traditional South Indian food in Mumbai with a homely touch and great value.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Fulsundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mutuswami Cafe is located just outside Dadar East railway station, so it’s very easy to find and perfect for a quick stop after travel. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, which is nice if you want to sit comfortably or just grab something quickly.
We tried the strawberry milkshake & mango milkshake both were thick, chilled, and refreshing. The paper masala dosa was big, crispy, and came with good chutney and sambar. Kanchipuram idli was soft and flavourful, a little different from regular idli and worth trying.
Cheese tava rice was spicy, cheesy, and filling good if you’re very hungry. We ended with pineapple sheera, which was warm, slightly sweet, and had a nice fruity taste.
Overall, it’s a good place for South Indian food and quick snacks near the station.

featured_reviews.name: VISHAL UPADHYAY

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re in Dadar and craving authentic South Indian flavors any time of the day, Muttuswami Cafe is the place to be!
This is the only café in the area open 24/7, making it a perfect spot for early breakfasts, late-night cravings, or casual meetups at any hour.
The food quality is outstanding, with every dish served fresh, flavorful, and satisfying:
Cheese Pav Bhaji – perfectly buttery with a generous layer of melted cheese that elevates the classic taste.
Podi Idli – soft, bite-sized idlis coated beautifully in spicy podi masala and ghee.
Muttuswami Special Benne Dosa – rich, crispy, and soaked in butter with a delicious traditional touch.
Spring Dosa – a unique fusion twist, crispy outside with a flavorful stuffed filling inside.
Fruit Custard Dessert – creamy, refreshing, and loaded with fresh fruits for the perfect sweet ending.
Their fresh juices are equally impressive — especially the pomegranate juice and the orange-mosambi mix, both refreshing and naturally sweet.
What truly makes the experience special is the warm and polite staff. The service is quick, attentive, and always delivered with a smile. The beautiful interiors create a clean, cozy, and welcoming atmosphere, making you want to sit back and enjoy your meal.

featured_reviews.name: Dr.Saranya Sasi
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited Sadanand Coffee House in Worli with high expectations, having heard about their good South Indian food. Unfortunately, my experience was a letdown from the start. Upon arrival, I was disappointed to find that they don't accept digital payments like Google Pay or Paytm, only cash or card. This seemed like a significant drawback in today's digital age. The food quality was another major disappointment. I ordered the Mysore Masala Dosa and Coconut Oothappam, but what I got was far from authentic. The dosa was dry and tasteless, with a meager spread of red chutney that didn't justify its name. The khara(red chutney), a crucial component of a traditional Mysore Dosa, was missing or replaced with something else entirely. The Coconut Oothappam was just average, lacking the freshness and flavor I've come to expect from this dish. To make matters worse, the service was slow,  our orders took a long time to arrive, and the Fresh Lime Soda we ordered was just okay. Overall, my experience at Sadanand Coffee House was underwhelming, with too many misses and not enough redeeming qualities. With some improvements in payment options, food authenticity, and service speed, this place could live up to its reputation. Until then, I'd think twice before returning.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A school friend sent me a reel about Poe and Pao in Chembur. I decided to go chasing Poe and Pao. Since I was already in Bandra, I thought I’d try their Matunga outlet instead.

Now, if you’re a true-blue Mumbaikar, you know traffic jams aren’t an inconvenience, they’re a lifestyle. So there I was, stuck in the middle of one, wishing for a restroom more than anything else.

When I finally reached, they said, “Go next door.” I stumbled into Dakshin Culture Curry and found the cleanest restroom in Mumbai. Small, but spotless. You can’t do pranayama there, but you’ll definitely come out feeling zen.

Feeling human again, I stepped out… and somehow found myself in Diva Maharashtracha. For a moment, I thought I’d taken a wrong turn in life. That’s when someone explained that Dakshin Culture Curry, Goa Portuguesa, and Diva Maharashtracha are a trilogy, same team, shared menu, different cuisines. And Poe and Pao? The latest addition to the family.

One look at the menu, and I knew there was no way I was walking back to Poe and Pao.

I started with a Sushegad Shot (feni, lime, and kaffir leaves) -  Goa in a glass. Then came the Khekade Kalimiri Soup, a crab-and-black-pepper combo that doubles as a natural sinus reliever. After that, Ravas Moile, Tender Coconut Cashew Nut Sukke (their signature dish), Chicken Modak, and Appam n Amboli.

The Chicken Modak was the surprise star—moist chicken kheema wrapped in a soft, pillowy coating. Though, between us, it did look slightly jaundiced.

They ended the meal with complimentary Caramel Custard—light, soft, and just the right sweetness.

The staff were courteous and attentive, the ambience warm and welcoming.

Ambience: A+
Food: A+++

What started as a quest for Poe and Pao turned into a delicious detour, a reminder that some of the best finds in Mumbai happen purely by serendipity.

Coming to the food — it was average at best. The Butter Chicken was unusually sweet, far from the regular taste, and the Mutton Rawalpindi was bland and lacked flavour.

That said, Shailendra’s service truly stood out. He was warm, attentive, knowledgeable about the menu, and even helped us warm milk for our little ones — a gesture we genuinely appreciated. If rating his service alone, it would be ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐.

featured_reviews.name: Raveena Gohil
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently dined at Copper Chimney during our trip to Mumbai, and it was an outstanding experience from start to finish. This legacy brand consistently delivers some of the best North Indian flavors you can find.
​
​Starters: The Stuffed Tandoori Aloo was perfectly seasoned, and the Paneer Tikka was incredibly soft with a wonderful smoky tandoori flavor.
​Mains: We ordered the Kadhai Paneer and Dal Makhani paired with Butter Naan and Rice. The Dal Makhani was exceptionally creamy and slow-cooked to perfection, while the Kadhai Paneer had the perfect balance of spices.
​Cocktails: The bar program is excellent. The Kokum Margarita was a fantastic, refreshing regional twist, and the Whiskey Sour was smooth and well-balanced.
​
The ambiance was lovely, cozy, and perfect for a relaxed dinner. The staff was professional, courteous, and ensured our food arrived fresh and hot.
​
Copper Chimney never fails to impress with its food quality and hospitality. It is absolutely worth every penny for a premium, authentic dining experience in Mumbai. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Ankan Singhal
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a lovely dining experience at Copper Chimney. I ordered the Paneer Khurchan along with lachcha paratha, missi roti, and rasmalai. The paneer was absolutely delicious—rich, flavorful, and well cooked. Lachcha paratha was soft and perfectly layered, a great combination with the curry. The missi roti, however, felt a bit dry compared to the rest of the meal. Ending on a sweet note, the rasmalai was really nice and is definitely a must-try. featured_reviews.name: Paras
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shiv Sagar is a brand that everyone has heard off. They have close to 18 Outlets in Mumbai.

The best part about it is that the consistency in taste remained across all its outlets, that it what stands out. I still think that the Pav bhaji here is one of the best in Mumbai.

Nachos with Cheese Sauce
Crispy Nachos with cheese sauce which had a very thick consistency which defines how well the cheese sauce was. Goes well with bell peppers.
Rating - 8/10

Paneer Butter Masala
NOPE, not what you are expecting. It was a very crispy dosa with crumbled paneer inside it and it had the normal Mashed Potato stuffing in it. Trust me it was DIVINE. The Dosa was crispy throughout and I could literally taste the butter. The Sambar was also delicious with the Tomato Chutney. ORDER IT!
Rating - 10/10

Paneer Makhmali Tikka
Makhmali Tikka generally contains Salt pepper and curd marination, this one also had sugar in it. Which really made it too sweet to consume. You can miss out on this one.
Rating - 3/10

Idli Chilli
OMG the quantity is like WOW. Typical Chinese flavour that you would expect from a Paneer Chilli. Just instead of Paneer here it was Idli and it was Crispy as well.
Rating - 9/10

Cheese Kadai Pav Bhaji
I like the Pav Bhaji (PB) to be DOUBLE spicy and he happily made it for me. So being a Kadai PB I was expecting it to come in some Handi but it was Khada Pav bhaji with exact same taste from normal PB. It was AMAZING still I will prefer normal PB over Kadai PB.
Rating - 10/10

Dal Tadka
One word to describe it. PERFECT. Tonnes of Garlic dumped inside it, exactly how I wanted it to be reason being - Garlic is BAE.
Rating - 10/10

Veg Kofta
Big chunks of Kofta waiting to be eaten up inside a very thick gravy made from lots of cashew paste and many other spices. The gravy was really atasty along with the Kofta but the only thing is it was too thick.
Rating - 8/10
Moong Dal Halwa
NOPE, it was made long ago and microwaved and served to me.
Rating - 6/10

Honorable Mention from Beverage section

Shiv Sagar Special Lassi
GO FOR IT! One of the BEST lassis' in town.
Rating - 10/10

Overall Rating - 4.5/5

featured_reviews.name: Enal Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located on the main street, the restaurant is easy to find but parking can be a challenge. The seating is well designed and comfortable, though it can get a bit noisy at times due to the traffic outside.
It’s a nice place if you want to try South Indian food with a fusion touch, while still having authentic options available. The idli was good, but the burnt garlic dosa absolutely won my heart.
The prices are slightly on the higher side for South Indian cuisine, possibly because of the prime location. The taste definitely justifies a visit, but I would rate it one star less purely because of the pricing.

featured_reviews.name: Kiara Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a lovely South Indian experience at this restaurant! The Tatte Idli was soft and fluffy, just the way we like it. The Chettinad Dosa was good, with a nice blend of spices, though it didn't blow us away.

The highlight was the Malabari Curry with Neer Dosa - a match made in heaven! The curry was rich and flavorful, and the Neer Dosa was light and soft.

Service was a bit slow, but the staff were polite, so that's a plus. The interior was cozy and welcoming, adding to the overall dining experience.

Overall, a great spot to try authentic South Indian cuisine. Will definitely go back for the Malabari Curry and Neer Dosa combo!"

featured_reviews.name: Kiyansh Shukla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vanakkam Vihar, located right opposite the iconic Royal Opera House in Girgaon, is a reliable, bustling spot for anyone craving solid, comforting South Indian comfort food in South Mumbai. Whether you are wrapping up a beach stroll at nearby Girgaon Chowpatty or stepping out after a show at the Opera House, this multi-level pure-vegetarian restaurant offers a welcoming and clean environment.
Here is a comprehensive look at what to expect:
The Vibe & Ambiance
The restaurant balances traditional charm with a modern, spacious casual-dining setup. The ground floor features comfortable high and low seating, while the upper level ("Firangi") branches out into multi-cuisine options. The space is well-lit, fully air-conditioned, and remarkably clean, making it highly family-friendly. The staff adds a touch of authenticity by dressing in traditional South Indian attire.
What to Order
While the massive menu extends to North Indian dishes and street-side snacks, the absolute highlight here remains their coastal and southern delicacies.
The Dosas: Their Kara Masala Dosa and Chettinad Dosa are beautifully crisp, served with generous portions of fresh coconut chutney, a tangy tomato-garlic chutney, and piping hot sambar. If you are looking for something lighter, the Neer Dosa and fluffy Appams paired with a rich veggie stew or Malabari curry are top-tier.
The Idli Platters: Beyond standard idlis, their Podi Idli (tossed in a vibrant, spiced gun powder and ghee) and the signature Thalaiva Idli are highly recommended.
Filter Coffee: No meal here is complete without their authentic Filter Coffee. It is served strong, perfectly frothy, and features that robust, traditional chicory-coffee blend.
Jain Options: For those with dietary restrictions, the restaurant stands out for offering a robust, dedicated selection of highly flavorful Jain South Indian variants.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A nice and cozy place to enjoy the meal. It is near the Girgaon Chowpatty and has the vibes of those south Indian restaurants.
The restaurant is spacious and can accommodate many visitors. It serves mostly the best South Indian Dishes and delicacies. A real big and fantastic menu awaits you as you occupy your place. It has plenty of varieties and offers great quality of food. We thoroughly enjoyed the Chettinad Dosa and Idly with gun powder ending with tea.
It is a great place to hang out with friends and family on a leisurely day. You won't regret the visit.
